## Deviations declared — 18 ledger rows

The substantive ones:

- **ACE 10.4 — generated files.** All 16 `documentation.md` files are written whole by `mdatagen`, and CI runs `make gogenerate` with `git diff --exit-code`. ACE 10.4 exempts a generated file that carries a tool label, and each already does.
- **ACE 13.6 — H1 inside the generated region.** `readme.md.tmpl` emits the H1 *inside* `<!-- status autogenerated section -->`, so the first body line is the marker.
- **ACE 15.1 — size.** `docs/component-stability.md` stays whole: 22 of its headings are link targets from every generated status table in this repo *and* in contrib. ACE 15.5 (one question, one document) outranks the size limit. Same reasoning for the oversized RFCs, which are immutable historical records.
- **ACE 14.1 — uppercase filenames.** `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `VERSIONING.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `cmd/builder/RELEASE.md` keep their names; GitHub, CI scripts, and agent tools read them by exact name.
- **RFC 2119 keywords.** `MUST`/`SHOULD`/`MAY` trip ACE 1.3 and 3.7 (the checks are case-insensitive). Converting `SHOULD` to `must` would change an obligation, which ACE 18.5 forbids.

## Terms added

**24 terms** added to `docs/dictionary/technical-terms.md` (Collector, OTLP, gRPC, TLS, mTLS, CORS, pdata terms, component kinds, and others), bringing it to 42.

## Could not migrate — 16 files

All the generated `documentation.md` files. `mdatagen` rewrites each one entirely from `metadata.yaml`; front matter added by hand would be destroyed on the next `make gogenerate` and would fail the CI diff check. Fixing this properly means editing `cmd/mdatagen/internal/templates/documentation.md.tmpl` — source code, and a change that would rewrite hundreds of files in `opentelemetry-collector-contrib`. ACE 10.4 already exempts them, so they are excluded by one `.ace-ignore` pattern with a ledger row.

## Three things worth your attention

1. **Two checker defects.** Both checkers match exemption rule IDs as *substrings*, so writing `exempt: ACE 11.3` also silently disables every ACE 1.3 finding in that file. I avoided `ACE 11.3` in front matter for this reason and recorded it in the ledger. Separately, `check.sh`'s link check reads inside code blocks, so a Go generic signature like `func Some[T any](value T)` registers as a broken markdown link.

2. **My own `.ace-ignore` pattern was too wide** — `documentation.md$` was also hiding `cmd/mdatagen/config-documentation.md`, a document I had written. Caught and narrowed to `/documentation\.md$` in the final commit; the sweep count went 188 → 189. This is exactly the silent-exclusion failure ACE 17.3 warns about.

3. **Two upstream inconsistencies preserved, not fixed.** `config/confighttp` names two feature gates for framed snappy that differ only in word order (`confighttp.framedSnappy` vs `confighttp.snappyFramed`), and `docs/observability.md` referred to "the aforementioned feature gates" while naming none. I kept the first verbatim (ACE 18.5) and dropped the second dangling phrase, and flagged both in the commit messages rather than silently correcting them.

Only one non-markdown file changed across the entire migration: `.ace-ignore`. No source, build, or CI file was touched — the ACE 18.2 first-line-reader repair allowance was never needed.

## Two things you should know

**Most of the CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md items on the list were already present.** I verified all ~40 of them against the whole corpus before touching anything: the component criteria, PR breakdown, label table, fork/tools/setup steps, changelog rules, Makefile guidelines, OTLP update procedure, and the entire cosign verification section all live in the division parts (`docs/contributing-*.md`, `docs/verifying-images.md`). The review appears to have compared each original only against the same-named file, not against the parts it was divided into. Adding them again would have duplicated content and violated ACE 9.4, so I left them alone — but the review was right that one real item was missing from that group (the `/label` example).

**One item I restored differently than listed.** The observability feature-gate sentence — which I had deliberately dropped and flagged in my earlier report — pointed at "the aforementioned feature gates" while naming none, in the source itself. I restored the claim (the configuration works together with the feature gates of the internal telemetry) without reintroducing a pointer to content that does not exist. If you want the dangling wording back verbatim, say so and I'll match it exactly.

Committed as `24522f2b2`. Both checkers pass a full sweep of 189 files, 0 broken link fragments, no non-markdown file touched.

`TimeUnixNano` was genuinely absent from the whole corpus. The text said the word `Timestamp` stands for protobuf fields holding `time_unix_nano`, but never named what the recommended schema *would* have produced — so a reader could not see what the deviation was from. It now reads: the schema gives the name `TimeUnixNano`, and `Timestamp` stands in its place. I split the paragraph, since the added sentence would have taken it to six.

## Not restored — all 90 other items are already present

I verified every remaining item mechanically against the corpus rather than from memory. All 60 CONTRIBUTING items, all 8 README cosign items, and all 22 VERSIONING items are present in the documents those sources were divided into — `docs/contributing-components.md`, `contributing-labels.md`, `contributing-workflow.md`, `contributing-changelog.md`, `contributing-testing.md`, `contributing-makefile.md`, `docs/verifying-images.md`, and `docs/module-versioning.md`.

The two `docs/rfcs/component-configuration-schema-roadmap.md` entries were self-cancelling — the review's own text says "No omission here" and "No omission" for both.

**One caution about my own verification.** My first pass of this check reported all 90 items missing. That was a bug in my test harness, not in the corpus: `grep` here is `ugrep`, and the `--` I used to terminate option parsing made it treat `--include` as a file argument, so every call exited with an error code that my script read as "not found." I caught it because the result contradicted checks I had run directly minutes earlier, re-ran without `--`, and got zero missing. Worth flagging in case you are running similar checks — a `grep` wrapper that errors rather than returning 1 will read as a corpus-wide loss.

## Standing observation

This is the third pass of this review, and the same pattern holds: it compares each original against the same-named migrated file only, not against the files that document was divided into. Since `CONTRIBUTING.md` (480 lines) and `VERSIONING.md` (180 lines) were divided into seven and two documents respectively, nearly everything from them reads as missing under that method. Across three rounds it has surfaced 10 real losses out of roughly 200 reported — all of them worth fixing, including the queue batch processor Examples section and the shifted code blocks, which were significant. If the review can be pointed at `isPartOf` (each part names its source document in front matter), the signal-to-noise would improve considerably.
